import Mathlib

inductive BinarySearchTree : Type
| Empty : BinarySearchTree
| Node : Int → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree

def view (t : BinarySearchTree) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => ∅
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}

def is_bst (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => True
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def search_precond (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  is_bst t
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Naive BST search, ignoring the invariant (which is only needed for correctness). -/
def searchAux (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) : Bool :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => false
  | BinarySearchTree.Node x l r =>
    if v = x then true
    else if v < x then searchAux l v
    else searchAux r v
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def search (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : search_precond t v) : Bool :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  searchAux t v
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def search_postcond (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) (result : Bool)
    (_ : search_precond t v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  result = (v ∈ view t)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem searchAux_correct (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) (h : is_bst t) :
    searchAux t v = true ↔ v ∈ view t := by
  induction t with
  | Empty => simp [searchAux, view]
  | Node x l r ihl ihr =>
    obtain ⟨hl, hbl, hr, hbr⟩ := h
    have ihl' := ihl hbl
    have ihr' := ihr hbr
    rw [searchAux]
    by_cases hvx : v = x
    · simp [hvx, view]
    · by_cases hlt : v < x
      · simp only [hvx, hlt, if_false, if_true, ihl', view, Set.mem_union,
          Set.mem_singleton_iff]
        constructor
        · intro hv; exact Or.inl (Or.inl hv)
        · rintro ((hv | hv) | hv)
          · exact hv
          · exact absurd (hr v hv) (by omega)
          · exact hv.elim
      · simp only [hvx, hlt, if_false, ihr', view, Set.mem_union,
          Set.mem_singleton_iff]
        constructor
        · intro hv; exact Or.inl (Or.inr hv)
        · rintro ((hv | hv) | hv)
          · exact absurd (hl v hv) (by omega)
          · exact hv
          · exact hv.elim
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem search_postcond_satisfied (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : search_precond t v) :
    search_postcond t v (search t v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  simp only [search_postcond, search, eq_iff_iff]
  exact searchAux_correct t v h_precond
  -- !benchmark @end proof

Verified — `LEAN VERIFIED` on check 2/15 (only unused-variable warnings, no errors, no `sorry`).

**Approach:**

- **auxcode** (`Solution.lean:29-37`): `searchAux` does the naive BST descent — compare `v` with the node value, recurse left if smaller, right if larger. It takes no proof argument, so it's plain structural recursion; the BST invariant is only needed for correctness, not for the definition.
- **code**: `search t v h_precond := searchAux t v`.
- **lemma**: `searchAux_correct` proves `searchAux t v = true ↔ v ∈ view t` under `is_bst t`, by induction on the tree. The interesting direction is completeness: when `v < x` the search only looks left, so the proof discharges the other branches using the invariant — any `y ∈ view r` satisfies `y > x`, contradicting `v < x` via `omega`, and `v = x` is already excluded. The `v > x` case is symmetric with the left-subtree bound.
- **proof**: the postcondition `result = (v ∈ view t)` coerces to a propositional equality `(search … = true) = (v ∈ view t)`, so `eq_iff_iff` turns it into the iff the lemma provides.

One note on a detail I hit: after `simp only [hvx, …]`, the singleton-membership disjunct `v = x` is rewritten to `False` rather than kept, so that branch closes with `hv.elim` instead of `absurd hv hvx`.
